description: Window function that numbers sessions: a new session starts when the gap since the previous event exceeds the interval.
comment: Order the window by the timestamp, ascending; IDs start at 1 in each partition. Rows that arrive out of timestamp order raise an error. The example returns 1, 1, 2.
example: SELECT ts, sessionize(ts, INTERVAL '30 minutes') OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS session_id FROM (VALUES (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:00'), (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:10'), (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 11:00')) t(ts);

description: Cohort retention: takes 2 to 32 boolean conditions and returns a BOOLEAN[] saying which of them were met in the group together with the first (anchor) condition.
Conversion funnel: returns how many steps (0 to N) were reached in order, within a time window that starts at the first step.
comment: Arguments: the window INTERVAL, an optional comma-separated mode string, the timestamp, then 1 to 32 step conditions. The example returns 2: the third step is more than an hour after the first.
example: SELECT window_funnel(INTERVAL '1 hour', ts, e = 'view', e = 'cart', e = 'buy') FROM (VALUES (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:00', 'view'), (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:05', 'cart'), (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 15:00', 'buy')) t(ts, e);

description: Like window_funnel, but returns the timestamps of the best funnel chain, one per step reached, as a list.
comment: Same arguments as window_funnel; the list is empty when the first step is never met. The example returns the timestamps of the first two steps.
example: SELECT window_funnel_events(INTERVAL '1 hour', ts, e = 'view', e = 'cart', e = 'buy') FROM (VALUES (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:00', 'view'), (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:05', 'cart'), (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 15:00', 'buy')) t(ts, e);

description: Returns true when the events contain a subsequence matching a pattern written as a mini-regex over condition references such as (?1).*(?2).
comment: Pattern steps are (?N), the wildcards . and .*, and time constraints such as (?t<=3600) in seconds. Events are sorted by timestamp first. The example returns true.
example: SELECT sequence_match('(?1).*(?2)', ts, e = 'view', e = 'buy') FROM (VALUES (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:00', 'view'), (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:05', 'cart'), (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:10', 'buy')) t(ts, e);

description: Counts the non-overlapping matches of a pattern in the events.
comment: Same pattern syntax as sequence_match. The example returns 2.
example: SELECT sequence_count('(?1).*(?2)', ts, e = 'view', e = 'buy') FROM (VALUES (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:00', 'view'), (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:05', 'buy'), (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:10', 'view'), (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:15', 'buy')) t(ts, e);

description: Returns the timestamps at which each (?N) step of a pattern was matched; when the pattern does not match completely, those of the longest partial chain.
comment: Same pattern syntax as sequence_match; the list is empty when no step is reached. The example returns the timestamps of the view and the buy.
example: SELECT sequence_match_events('(?1).*(?2)', ts, e = 'view', e = 'buy') FROM (VALUES (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:00', 'view'), (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:05', 'cart'), (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:10', 'buy')) t(ts, e);

description: Returns the value of the event next to a matched chain of events (the following one going forward, the preceding one going backward), or NULL when there is none.
comment: Arguments: direction ('forward' or 'backward'), base ('head', 'tail', 'first_match' or 'last_match'), the timestamp, the value column, the base condition, then 1 to 32 event conditions. Follows ClickHouse's sequenceNextNode. The example returns cart.
example: SELECT sequence_next_node('forward', 'first_match', ts, e, e = 'view', e = 'view') FROM (VALUES (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:00', 'view'), (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:05', 'cart'), (TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 10:10', 'buy')) t(ts, e);

description: Returns the version of the loaded behavioral extension.
